title: The Ember of the Sundered Sea
premise: Bram Okafor flees his master's cottage the night the valley's wards fail and the stars vanish, discovering that the valley itself is a spell—a pocket country erased from the world by his own bloodline generations ago. Guided by a disgraced cartographer, a dragon's last ember kept in a lantern, and a found family of outcasts, Bram learns he is the heir to the wards and must choose between restoring the valley's comforting lie and telling the truth that will unmake it. In the climax he carries the ember to the Sundered Sea and relights the stars at the cost of the valley's existence, opening a door for his people into the real world. The book ends with Bram, no longer invisible, leading the valley folk across a border that finally exists.
about_author: Mirabel Eastwick is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper's daughter who grew up mapping coastlines that no longer appear on modern charts. She writes fantasies about borders, inheritance, and the families we build when the old maps fail.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. On the eve of his escape from Mistress Halden's cottage, the valley's stars vanish and the border wards shudder and fall. Bram runs anyway, terrified and exhilarated, and the emotional beat is the vertigo of a wish granted in the worst possible way.

chapters.title: Hedge-Witch's Boy
chapters.summary: Flashback-woven chapter in Bram's POV establishing his apprenticeship, his master's secrecy about the valley's edge, and the scar on his palm that itches near the wards. The beat is the ache of belonging to someone who lies to you.

chapters.title: The Cartographer of Nothing
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the valley's edge he finds Ilsa Vane, a disgraced royal cartographer, sketching a border that her instruments refuse to record. She reveals the valley appears on no map. The beat is the first crack of wonder: the world is bigger than his fear.

chapters.title: A Lantern Full of Fire
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She carries the Ember—a dragon-fire shard that is the last light of the extinguished stars—and admits she was hired to steal it and failed. The beat is guilt disguised as pragmatism as she decides Bram is useful rather than a burden.

chapters.title: What the Valley Forgot
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Ember reacts to Bram's blood, and Ilsa realizes he is descended from the Sunderers who cast the valley out of the world. The beat is betrayal: his whole identity was a ward's construction.

chapters.title: The Company of the Unmapped
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, Bram's POV. They gather companions: Tam, a ward-tinkerer exiled for asking questions; Old Sef, a fisherman who remembers the sea; and Wren, a child born the night the stars went out. The beat is the fragile first warmth of found family.

chapters.title: Doors That No Longer Open
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The company seeks the historical Gate of Return, only to find it sealed from the inside—by Bram's ancestors, deliberately. The beat is the horror of inheritance as a cage built with love.

chapters.title: The Tinkerer's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam explains the valley's magic is a memory of magic, sustained by the wards and dying since the stars went out. The beat is grief for a homeland that turns out to be a beautifully maintained illusion.

chapters.title: Riders of the Hollow March
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Wardens of the valley—guardians who believe the outside world is a devouring void—ambush the company. Bram's blood-mark spares him, and the wardens mark him a traitor. The beat is the cost of choosing truth over loyalty.

chapters.title: Old Sef Remembers the Water
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Sef tells of the Sundering: the valley's founders fleeing a war, paying a dragon to erase them from the world. The Ember is the dragon's heart-fire, its last payment. The beat is the weight of stories as inheritance.

chapters.title: Wren Asks About Stars
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, childlike and piercing. Wren, born starless, asks why anyone would want the valley back if it means the sky stays dark. The beat is innocence cutting through the adults' nostalgia.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa's former employer, the magister Corvane, catches up and offers to restore the valley's stars in exchange for Bram's blood to bind the wards forever—under his control. The beat is temptation dressed as mercy.

chapters.title: What Mistress Halden Knew
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The wardens deliver Halden to Corvane, and Bram learns his master raised him as a living key, a contingency plan she never had the heart to use. The beat is the collapse of the last safe love he had.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Hollow March
chapters.summary: Ensemble, Tam's POV. A running battle through the dying valley, where unmapped places are literally unraveling into blankness. Sef is lost holding a crossing. The beat is mourning that cannot pause.

chapters.title: The Ember Grows Cold
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The Ember dims, and Wren—star-born—is the only one who can hear its voice: the dragon is not dead, only forgotten, and it will answer to its heir. The beat is responsibility arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Corvane's Perfect Country
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. He reveals his plan: a valley restored and eternal, with him as warden-king and its people as a preserved museum. The beat is chilling sincerity—he genuinely believes he is saving them.

chapters.title: The Door Out of a Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Following the Ember's fading pulse, the company finds the true Gate: not a place but a choice, sealed inside the bloodline's memory. Bram must relive the founders' Sundering to unlock it. The beat is terror and acceptance.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Climax, Bram's POV. At the Sundered Sea, Corvane attacks as Bram feeds his blood and his truth to the Ember. The dragon's fire relights the stars, and the valley's illusion burns away. The beat is sacrifice: to save everyone, he must end the world he was born in.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Valley
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. The valley dissolves; its people, waking, stand at the sea's edge facing a real sky for the first time. Corvane, unmade by the truth he refused, is gone. The beat is stunned, collective grief and awe.

chapters.title: Mapping the Way Through
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa draws the first honest map of the passage out, and Tam builds a road where her lines run. The beat is purpose reborn from ruin—making a way is its own kind of magic.

chapters.title: The Border That Exists
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The valley folk cross into the world; some turn back to build a new settlement by the sea rather than leave. Halden, freed and forgiven, chooses to stay with them. The beat is reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: Emberlight
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, epilogue. Under restored stars, Bram keeps the Ember as a hearth-flame for the sea-settlement, Wren sees her first constellation, and his scar no longer itches. The beat is quiet belonging: found family, an honest map, a door left open.
